observations.feature: Potential high-speed solar wind stream from coronal holes
observations.detail: Coronal holes visible in AIA 193 Å may be sources of high-speed streams, but geoeffectiveness and arrival timing cannot be determined from this image alone.

assessment.risk_reasoning: Current geomagnetic conditions are quiet (Kp = 2.0) with no NOAA space weather scales in effect. No Earth-directed CME can be confirmed from a single AIA image, and no geomagnetic storm forecast is provided. Although relativistic electron flux is elevated (a satellite charging concern rather than a direct drag driver) and coronal holes are visible, there is no indication of enhanced atmospheric density that would significantly increase LEO drag over the next 72 hours.

trace.policy_text: Manoeuvre when Pc >= 1e-4 and a verified option exists. Between 1e-5 and 1e-4, or when Pc is diluted, prefer getting precise data if there is time before the latest safe burn. On public TLE data, do not decide a burn while there is time to get precise ephemeris; TLE screening finds candidates, it does not decide manoeuvres. Never manoeuvre if our propulsion status is unverified. If the other object is an active satellite that can manoeuvre, contact its operator before moving; if it is an operational satellite whose capability is unknown, notify its operator. Keep at least 30 minutes for command upload. Max 1.0 m/s per burn.

report.subject: ESCALATION: Conjunction 60454 vs 61786 at 2026-10-25T00:34:27Z — Pc 0.0729, verified burns O1/O2, other operator capability unknown, decision deadline 2026-10-24T21:41:13Z
report.body: Conjunction between our satellite NORAD 60454 (EOS-08) and NORAD 61786 (SITRO-AIS 38) predicted at 2026-10-25T00:34:27Z with miss distance 0.0166 km, relative speed 13.39 km/s. Pc = 0.07291984448273788 (simulated precise ephemeris). This exceeds the policy threshold of 1e-4 (red level). Two verified burn options exist: O1 (prograde, 0.1484 m/s, burn at 2026-10-24T22:11:13Z, lead 143.2 min, miss after 2.0 km) and O2 (prograde, 0.8209 m/s, burn at 2026-10-25T00:06:44Z, lead 27.7 min, miss after 2.0 km). Both passed rescreen (711 objects, no new close approaches). The other object is an operational satellite (Sitronics Group, Russia) with maneuver capability unknown. Policy requires notifying the operator of an operational satellite with unknown capability before we maneuver. The agent coded policy route was COORDINATE O1; the model route was COORDINATE; the validator overrode to ESCALATE because the two decision routes disagree and a person should decide. We cannot act autonomously because coordination with the other operator is required and their intent is unknown. The latest feasible burn that satisfies the 30-minute command-upload minimum is O1 at 2026-10-24T22:11:13Z, giving a decision deadline of 2026-10-24T21:41:13Z (burn time minus 30 min). Current time is 2026-10-24T21:34:27Z, leaving ~7 minutes.
